review_notes: I read the whole file. I compared its two hand-built bundled `DFinsupp`s with the existing `DFinsupp.mapRange` and `DFinsupp.zipWith` in Mathlib/Data/DFinsupp/Defs.lean. I also checked the pointwise `Finset` zero API (`singleton_zero`, `singletonZeroHom`) and the analogous `Finsupp` file. `Finset.dfinsupp` is already an embedding built with `Finset.map`, and the `LocallyFiniteOrder` instance is built with `ofIcc`, so I found nothing to flag there. Only the `DFinsupp.mapRange` and `DFinsupp.zipWith` constructors apply to the two findings. I did not assess `DFinsupp.mapRange.addMonoidHom` or `Finset.singletonAddMonoidHom`, because they need `AddMonoid`/`AddZeroClass` and the file only assumes `Zero`. Nothing was compiled, so the proposed replacements are untested. The reuse depends on `0 : Finset (α i)` (the pointwise zero, which is `{0}`) unfolding definitionally, which the file already relies on. The `singleton` finding has the weaker practical benefit, because `DFinsupp.singleton` has no other uses in Mathlib.

findings.problem: `DFinsupp.singleton` is the pointwise image of `f` under `Finset.singleton`, which sends `0` to `0 = {0}` in the pointwise `Finset` zero. That is exactly what `DFinsupp.mapRange` provides. Instead the file proves the support-witness field by hand and only gets the apply lemma by `rfl`. The result does not reuse the `mapRange` API (`mapRange_apply`, `mapRange_zero`, `mapRange_def`, `support_mapRange`). Mathlib already supplies the zero-preservation fact as `Finset.singleton_zero` and the bundled `Finset.singletonZeroHom`.
findings.proposed_change: Define `def singleton (f : Π₀ i, α i) : Π₀ i, Finset (α i) := f.mapRange (fun _ => Finset.singleton) (fun _ => Finset.singleton_zero)`, using the existing `Finset.singleton_zero`. Here `Finset.singleton` is the function `a ↦ {a}`. Then `mem_singleton_apply_iff` can be proved via `mapRange_apply`/`mem_singleton`. A `support_singleton_subset` lemma would follow from `support_mapRange`.
findings.benefit: This removes a manual `Multiset`-level support proof. It shows that `singleton` is a `mapRange`, and it gives `mapRange_zero`, `support_mapRange` and the other `mapRange` lemmas for free. It also makes `singleton` agree with the `Finset.singletonZeroHom` structure instead of re-deriving the same zero-preservation.

findings.problem: `rangeIcc f g` is a pointwise binary operation on two `DFinsupp`s with `Icc 0 0 = 0 = {0}`. That is exactly the situation `DFinsupp.zipWith` handles. The file re-proves the support-witness construction by hand (sum of the two multisets, two `Multiset.notMem_mono` arguments, then `Icc_self`). This is the same construction as `zipWith`. As a result, it does not reuse the `zipWith` API (`zipWith_apply`, `zipWith_def`).
findings.proposed_change: Define `def rangeIcc (f g : Π₀ i, α i) : Π₀ i, Finset (α i) := DFinsupp.zipWith (fun _ => Icc) (fun _ => Icc_self 0) f g`, using `Icc_self : Icc a a = {a}` (the existing `Icc_self` lemma) and `{0} = 0` by `rfl`. Then `rangeIcc_apply` stays `rfl` (or `zipWith_apply`). `support_rangeIcc_subset` can be derived from `zipWith_def` as `mk_support_subset`, or kept as is.
findings.benefit: This removes about ten lines of low-level `Multiset` support reasoning. It makes explicit that `rangeIcc` is the `zipWith` of `Icc`, and the existing `zipWith` lemmas apply to it. It also parallels the neighbouring `singleton` definition, which would be a `mapRange`.
